Alicia — great meeting, appreciate the clarity on your MRP profile. Post-call recap and what we will deliver by EOD Friday (our timezone):

1) Quick answers up front:
- Hosted per-1M tokens (baseline): $210 — this assumes batching around 8 requests/batch, median seq len ~220 tokens, and a platform-level L2 prefix/KV cache hit of 18%.
- Hyperscaler managed endpoint estimate (like S3-based model hosting with autoscaling): ~$360 per-1M tokens for the same workload (different batching efficiency and higher networking/serialization overhead).
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem): unit cost converges toward hosted with a ~5-10% uplift for dedicated infra + longer-term support overhead; we can run a tailored TCO if you prefer committed capacity pricing.

2) Differentiators that drove the delta:
- Smart routing & model variants: we route by cost/latency policy and fall back to quantized variants automatically — reduces tail spend without manual intervention.
- KV/prefix caching: automatic cache population across similar sessions; in many workloads we see 15-30% token reduction vs. naive serving.
- Fine-grained batching control: avoids latency spikes by adaptive batching thresholds driven by SLAs.

3) Deliverables (we will attach):
- redwood-econ-vs-hyperscaler.xlsx: per-1M token breakdown, sensitivity knobs (batch size, cache hit %).
- MAP-1M-token-scenarios.pdf: a short slide with recommended test matrix.
- A short benchmark runbook + minimal scripts for Vectoria to execute (24-hour microbench).

4) Proposed quick test plan (low lift):
- 24h run, three traffic patterns: interactive (p50 latency target 200ms), bursty (spikes to 200rps), and batch (bulk embeddings/async).
- Metrics: tokens processed, avg/p95 latency, batch size distribution, cache hit %, cost / 100k tokens.
- Acceptance: p95 latency within agreed SLO and host per-1M below hyperscaler baseline.

Next steps:
- We will share the two attachments and the runbook now.
- Ben to propose specific dates for a 24h microbench with your infra contact.
- Karthik will propose the precise telemetry fields to capture for apples-to-apples comparison.

I'll follow up with a short spreadsheet and the runbook in the next message.
